# Campaign Channel Discovery

- Discovery is operator-triggered background work, single-flighted per campaign; the operator names the accounts that read (`account_ids`, required — the server no longer auto-picks the listener). Reservation is all-or-nothing: every picked account is checked against one fleet snapshot, then locked in sorted id order under warming's per-account lifecycle lock and re-asked from BOTH owners inside it; the first failing account refuses the whole start and is named in the outcome. Warming, the listener and a run exclude each other symmetrically; a neuroshilling campaign sits outside that circle. Do not hold the lifecycle locks across the run.
- The reserved accounts form one pool. Waves take the next account round-robin; recommendation and post-page reads prefer a Premium account still in rotation (a non-premium account receives FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT there and a tenth of the recommendations). Each account may spend at most `discovery_max_reads_per_run` wave reads — past that it is skipped for wave reads (truncation, not a stop) but stays in the pool for probes, which are bounded by `limit` instead. An account that floods, cools or fails `discovery_max_consecutive_errors` times in a row leaves too; the run stops only when the pool is empty, labelled by the reason the last account left. Health is re-read from the in-process cooldown before every read. Reads stay sequential: no fan-out.
- Sources: keyword search, the global post search (paged, narrower than its docs suggest), recommendations for the operator's seed and for the sweep's best CHANNEL hits — recommendations return channels only, so a groups search skips both recommendation waves as `kind_unsupported`. A chosen category appends its word bundle to the sweep. `kind` is decided once, at the gateway. `hide_seen` and `limit` act in the merge; `seen` is keyed by the case-folded handle and written at the END of a run over the rows the board shows, never before qualification. A re-run whose every hit is already seen keeps the previous rows instead of wiping them. `language`, `comments`, `access` open-vs-join-request and `category` need `about`/`join_request` from GetFullChannel: the linked-group cache stores both, so a fresh row settles from cache through the same admission as a probe and only a legacy row missing the fact is probed. A rejected row is DELETED, never stored hidden; counts land in the run report's `filtered`. Unknown values never reject (an access the probe could not establish is `None`, not `open`); groups are never rejected by the comments filter (they have no verdict) and are shown `not_adoptable`. A username-less recommendation is stored as `id:<channel_id>` with access `subscription`, never probed, never adoptable, and rejected by `comments = on`. Subscriber bounds apply once counts are known, never to recommendation seeds. An unresolvable seed is a refusal, never an empty answer.
- A run's waves share one read budget of `discovery_max_reads_per_run × pool size`, spent in wave order (keywords → the operator's seed → post pages → recommendations); the operator's seed does not queue behind an automatic wave; recommendation reads are held back before the post pages. The post wave caps its own total. Truncation is reported and is NOT a run error. The rolling-24h search allowance is separate. Wave shape is a module literal, not a setting; the candidate cap is the request's `limit` alone.
- Whether a read failure is a rate limit is the gateway's `kind`, never the reason text; a limit with no duration takes the configured no-duration cooldown.
- Merge interleaves per OUTCOME, not per source, before the cap: source priority decides dedup spelling, not which source fills the cap.
- Every source reports `ran`/`failed`/`skipped`; `hits` are DISTINCT usable channels. Replace stored candidates only when at least one source answered; an EMPTY result additionally needs the keyword sweep itself to have answered and nothing dropped as seen. A run stopped by a flood or a cooldown never displaces the stored set. Per-run progress, provenance and verdict fields are ephemeral across restart; `kind`, the seen table and the cached `about`/`join_request` are the persisted exceptions.
- Keyword suggestion is a convenience beside the box, not part of a run: no campaign, no account, no Telegram read; single WORDS (the SPA tokenises on whitespace and commas); DeepSeek only; an unusable answer is a 200 carrying a code.
